method: Complete reads of two pinned files, verified Git blob/SHA256; compiled unchanged HighwayHash implementation and authored streaming-consistency harness.
findings: Low-level API requires32-byte packets and remainder length1..31; remainder zero must not be passed because rotation assumes nonzero count. One-shot path guards remainder call with size&31.

Streaming API buffers partial packets and flushes complete packets. CatFinish copies hash state before processing remainder/final permutations, enabling repeated finish without consuming live state; low-level finalize mutates state.
Byte loading explicitly assembles little-endian64-bit lanes; output APIs return integer words, so external serialization still needs an explicit byte-order contract.
Header usage example calls HighwayHashCatFinish64(state) instead of passing address; implementation declaration requires pointer. Documentation example is not an executed API test.
